resumen: A step back until the rear knee is close to the floor, and back up. The front foot never moves, so the knee takes less load than in a forward lunge.
ejecucion: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, hanging at your sides.
Step back with one leg and land on the ball of your foot.
Bend both knees until the back one is a hand-span from the floor.
The front knee stays over the foot, which has not moved at any point.
Push through the front leg to come back up, and alternate sides.
matices: The comparison with the forward lunge is measured: in the cited study the backward version produced less quadriceps force, less kneecap loading and less knee flexion. That makes it kinder to a sensitive knee, not "better": the stimulus is somewhat smaller too.
